html:<strong>Begrænset udbud.</strong> D: Limited supply. There's only limited room to build new housing in the central districts, so when demand rises, it's the prices rather than the number of homes that get pushed up.
html:<strong>Regn på den konkrete adress: Calculate for the specific address. The price per square metre varies enormously from Indre By to Valby. Our page on property investment in Copenhagen gathers market data and yields for the capital.
html:<strong>Sammenlign med resten af ma: Compare with the rest of the market. Use the Deal Engine to compare a Copenhagen flat against deals in, say, Aarhus or Funen, so you can see what you're really paying for the location.
html:<strong>Skil værdistigning fra cash: Separate value growth from cashflow. Look at both parts separately. If the cashflow is negative, be honest that the return depends on prices continuing to rise.
html:<strong>Stigende efterspørgsel.</st: Rising demand. More people want to live in and around the capital — jobs, education and urbanisation are all pulling in the same direction.
html:<strong>Stress-test værdistigningen: Stress-test the value growth. What happens to your total gain if the increase is ⟦0⟧% a year instead of ⟦1⟧%? An analysis tool shows IRR and total return over the entire ownership period, not just year ⟦2⟧.
html:De københavnske ejerlejligheder bli: Copenhagen owner-occupied flats keep pulling ahead — but high value growth and low ongoing yield are two sides of the same coin. The savvy investor doesn't buy into a story that "Copenhagen always rises"; he crunches the numbers on the specific deal and knows exactly where the money comes from. Start by analysing a flat — and within seconds you'll know whether it's a bet on value growth or a genuine investment.
html:Den stærke værdistigning er attrakt: The strong value growth is attractive if your strategy is long-term wealth building. But there's a catch: in the central postcodes, the price per square metre is often DKK ⟦0⟧-⟦1⟧, which means the gross yield is rarely above ⟦2⟧-⟦3⟧%. With a ⟦4⟧% down payment, a typical Copenhagen deal therefore runs with negative monthly cashflow — you pay to own, betting on the value growth instead.
html:Det er ikke nødvendigvis en dårlig: It's not necessarily a bad deal — but it's a different type of deal to a cashflow property in the provinces, and you need to know what you're buying. The difference between the two is at the heart of our overview of investment strategies, and you'll find the concepts behind the numbers in the glossary.
html:Kombinationen betyder, at prisudvik: The combination means that future price growth for Copenhagen owner-occupied flats may outpace the general trend — exactly as we've seen over the past decade.
html:Mens boligpriserne på landsplan ven: While national house prices are expected to rise ⟦0⟧-⟦1⟧% in ⟦2⟧, the Danish central bank points out that Copenhagen owner-occupied flats will continue to rise faster than the rest of the country. For investors, this is both an opportunity and a trap: the value growth is strong, but the high prices push the yield to the floor. Here's why the capital stands out — and how to work out whether a flat in Copenhagen is actually a good investment.
